text:
When I moved my side project's database onto a 2 GB VPS, I assumed Postgres would cope. It has a reputation for being sturdy, and my dataset was small. I hadn't counted on how fast memory runs out when you leave the defaults alone and let the application open as many connections as it wants.

I followed the usual advice and set shared_buffers to 512 MB, a quarter of the machine's RAM, and that part was fine. The trouble was that the app could open up to 200 client connections, and each backend process uses its own memory. That left the server with very little headroom, and the kernel noticed. In the first month the OOM killer ran three times, and each time it took Postgres down.

What helped most was less clever than any tuning parameter. I put pgbouncer in front of the database, which cut the connection count from 200 to 20, and the application never noticed.

This post covers what went wrong, what I changed, and what I'd do before running Postgres on a small server again.
